- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for risk premium or panic-driven rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter or reduce peak forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizon.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 7-day average is > 10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with trend correction.
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 0.0 → 0.4 → 0.6), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak unless confirmed by technical indicators.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome exceeds model by > 5% in 3 consecutive days, adjust next forecast downward by 2–4% to avoid overfitting to recent momentum.
- If model forecast is > 10% above true outcome for 2+ consecutive days, apply “reversion penalty” — reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence with historical mean.
